top.title: Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and sports broadcaster, dies at 75
top.description: Former football star and famed broadcaster Tom Jackson has died, his family and ESPN announced Sunday. Jackson rose to prominence as a Denver Broncos player and went on to build a career as a beloved NFL analyst for ESPN, becoming a mainstay of the network's Sunday football programs for three decades, including its "Sunday NFL Countdown" show. He was 75. Jimmy Pitaro, the chairman of ESPN, praised Jackson in a statement released by the network after his death. In it, Pitaro called Jackson "one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN's history," who "brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans." "Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends," Pitaro said. "Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure." Jackson's family informed ESPN that he died Friday, but it was their wish that his death not be announced until the start of the network's "Sunday NFL Countdown" show by Jackson's longtime friend and on-air partner Chris Berman. "Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom's was frequent and unmistakable," Berman said at the start of the show. "Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend, too." Berman said Jackson made a surprise visit a couple of weeks ago to ESPN, where he worked for 32 years after playing 14 seasons for the Broncos, and that the two talked on Tuesday. A fourth-round draft pick out of Louisville in 1973, Jackson was the inspirational leader of Denver's first Super Bowl team in 1977. He started 177 games for the Broncos between 1973-86, retiring after the team's second Super Bowl appearance. He was a two-time Associated Press All-Pro and three-time Pro Bowler. Following his playing days, Jackson had a second career at ESPN from 1987-2016 and was featured on "Sunday NFL Countdown" and "NFL Primetime." Before the internet and NBC took over the Sunday night package in 2006, "NFL Primetime" was must-see viewing for fans and players because it showed highlights from all the games, as well as the interplay between Berman and Jackson, who often finished each other's sentences. top.title: ‘Shocking’: Draymond Green says it’s ‘crazy’ after watching what Giannis Antetokounmpo did
top.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Giannis Antetokounmpo leaving the Milwaukee Bucks for the Miami Heat was the blockbuster deal of the summer. The Greek Freak spent over a decade with the Bucks, led them to an NBA championship and became one of the biggest superstars in the game during his time in Milwaukee. Yet, he chose not to shake hands with his old teammates recently, which shocked many people, including Draymond Green. Draymond Green reacts to Giannis Antetokounmpo snubbing former Bucks teammates Antetokounmpo faced the Milwaukee Bucks for the first time since his move to the Miami Heat, and he emerged victorious. The Heat won 137-130, with their big man scoring 27 points and recording 14 rebounds and nine assists in what was a scintillating display. After the game, Antetokounmpo was seen leaving the court without shaking hands with his former Bucks teammates. That was surprising, to say the least, not just for us fans but for fellow pros like Green as well. Speaking about the incident on his YouTube show, the Golden State Warriors star expressed his shock and suggested that there may have been some problems behind the scenes. He said: “A little surprised that Giannis ain’t shake the hands of any of his teammates. That was interesting to me, because those are guys that you’ve been going to war with. “And even if you don’t like something with the organisation, something that could’ve happened, you went to war with those guys. Giannis is one of those guys who brought his teammates to Greece. He’s a leader. “So to lead them guys and those guys followed your lead, and then to those very guys who followed his lead to now say nothing to them… “Unless something was going on in their locker room where he felt like guys turned their backs on him, which I’m not in their locker room, I don’t know. But I think that’s a little shocking. Like, that’s a little crazy to me.” We don’t know what Antetokounmpo’s relationship with the Bucks is like anymore, but he must be happy with his decision to leave Milwaukee. The Greek star has been brilliant with the Miami Heat, who, after a poor start, have begun to look like serious contenders. The Bucks, on the other hand, have won just one of their first 17 games and are at rock bottom in the Eastern Conference standings. top.description: FC Barcelona v Villarreal CF - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona manager Hansi Flick expressed deep frustration with the match officials following his side's dramatic 3-2 victory over Villarreal on Sunday. Despite witnessing a spirited comeback from two goals down, the German tactician was left fuming at the treatment his coaching staff received on the touchline. Flick vents fury at touchline scrutiny Flick did not hold back in his assessment of the officiating during Barcelona's narrow win over Villarreal , specifically targeting the conduct of the fourth official after being shown a yellow card for his protests and seeing substitute Fermin Lopez sent off from the bench in the 74th minute. According to referee Hernandez Hernandez's post-match report, the midfielder was dismissed for approaching the fourth official and protesting loudly, repeatedly saying 'Don't mess with me!', before heading straight down the tunnel prior to being shown the red card. 'The fourth official was only looking at our bench,' Flick stated during his post-match press conference. He expressed confusion over the lack of communication from the officiating crew, noting that he was sanctioned simply for asking questions about the game's flow. 'He has to help the referee on the field and he only looked at us. We will see what information they give us. I asked and they gave me a yellow card,' he said. The tension between the Barcelona bench and referee Hernandez Hernandez was a running theme throughout the afternoon. Flick admitted that the history and reputation of the officiating crew preceded the match, leading to an expectant but frustrated atmosphere. 'If it had been another result, maybe I wouldn't say anything, but today we knew which referee there was and we expected this. I am happy with the referees in general, but not with him. The linesman and the fourth official were very aware of us. You can do it differently, they could have talked to us, but they haven't told us anything,' the Blaugrana boss added. Early errors haunt the Blaugrana While the officiating was a major talking point, Flick was also quick to highlight the defensive lapses that saw Barcelona endure a catastrophic opening, conceding twice inside the first seven minutes through Thierno Barry and Tani Oluwaseyi - the first time the Blaugrana had shipped two goals that early in a league fixture since a clash with Real Zaragoza in November 1981. 'They got ahead in the first two plays. The first goal was a clear mistake of ours and they scored directly,' Flick remarked when analysing the nightmare start. However, he was full of praise for how his players reacted to the adversity, showing significant character to regroup before the interval even after missing a penalty that could have simplified the comeback much earlier. top.title: Kirk Cousins on pace to make unique NFL history
top.description: Nov 24, 2022; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) warms up before the game against the New England Patriots at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-USA TODAY Sports Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins has had a whirlwind month, getting traded from the Las Vegas Raiders back to the franchise where he spent six seasons. Now, that midseason move has put the veteran in position to do something no quarterback has ever done before. Because the Raiders hadn’t yet had their bye week and the Vikings already had theirs, Cousins is on track to become the first quarterback in the modern era to play 18 regular-season games. So far, the 38-year-old reportedly has no objection to the unique opportunity to make NFL history. Cousins Returns to Minnesota The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Raiders just hours before this month’s NFL trade deadline, sending a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas in return. The deal brought the four-time Pro Bowler back to Minnesota, where he played from 2018 to 2023, and put him in line to start for the Vikings right away. It also cleared the way for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take over as the starter in Las Vegas. Cousins had played the first nine games of the season for the Raiders while mentoring the rookie, and star wide receiver Justin Jefferson said that Cousins immediately took charge after rejoining the Vikings. His return got off to a strong start, too. Cousins threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns last Sunday as the Vikings rolled to a 30-10 win over the rival Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Across 10 combined games with Las Vegas and Minnesota, Cousins has completed 64.5% of his passes for 2,547 yards and 22 touchdowns. That has him sixth in the NFL in passing yards and tied with C.J. Stroud for second in touchdown passes, trailing only Joe Burrow’s 27. ‘Hasn’t had a bye week’ The Raiders don’t have their bye until Week 13, while the Vikings already had theirs back in Week 6. That leaves Cousins with no week off this season and a chance to suit up 18 times, starting with Sunday’s game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. That will allow Cousins to make some rather unique NFL history. No quarterback has ever played 18 regular-season games, but a handful of other players have. According to the Elias Sports Bureau, the only players to do it since 1930 are Leonard Williams (2023), Mike Williams (2024), Rashid Shaheed (2025), and Dre’Mont Jones (2025). Some teams have gone out of their way to avoid that situation. The Jacksonville Jaguars rested Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis last week after acquiring them from the Atlanta Falcons and Philadelphia Eagles, respectively, since both players would have otherwise lost their bye weeks. Cousins’ situation hasn’t gone unnoticed around the league, either. top.title: Real Madrid forward not guaranteed a starting spot under Mourinho despite encouraging signs
top.description: Real Madrid forward not guaranteed a starting spot under Mourinho despite encouraging signs In recent weeks, there has been a lot of noise surrounding Vinicius Jr. and his slow start to the season at Real Madrid. Coupled with the impressive performances of summer signing Yan Diomande, there have been question marks over the Brazilian international’s place in the starting lineup. But the 26-year-old seems to be recovering his form as he starred for Brazil during the recent international break and then impressed in his cameo in Real Madrid’s 2-1 win over Celta Vigo last night. No guaranteed spot for Vinicius However, despite the encouraging signs from Vinicius, Defensa Central reports that Jose Mourinho has no intention of restoring him to Real Madrid’s starting lineup simply because of his status at the club. Vinicius was left on the bench vs Celta Vigo. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Instead, the Portuguese tactician plans to rotate the superstar winger with Diomande on the left flank in both La Liga and the UEFA Champions League, with selection based on performances rather than reputation. Mourinho wants Vinicius to rediscover his peak form without interrupting Diomande’s development, particularly after the Ivorian’s impressive performances have made him a strong contender for regular minutes. There may also be occasions when the two wingers feature together, with Diomande moving to the right. Vinicius determined to win back his place Vinicius has been a regular starter for Real Madrid for several years and has already won major honours at the club. Being asked to share his position not something he is accustomed to. Vinicius will have to share minutes with Yan Diomande. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) However, Diomande has given Mourinho plenty of reasons to trust him, not only due to his attacking contributions, but also with the way he helps out the team off the ball. The Brazilian international is aware that his younger teammate has earned the trust of the manager and the support of the fans. But he remains determined to re-establish himself as a regular starter for Los Blancos . Vinicius understands what he needs to do to regain his place, with improvements needed in his physical condition while he works to regain his confidence following a difficult spell. For now, though, he will have to settle for sharing minutes with Diomande, as the coach plans on giving both players opportunities rather than guaranteeing either a place.

top.title: A Lim Kim Holds One-Shot Lead As Nelly Korda Closes Gap
top.description: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images A Lim Kim survived a shaky finish to keep a one-shot lead heading into Sunday at the CME Group Tour Championship. The rain-soaked Tiburon Golf Club in Naples, Florida, presented a difficult course for the field. Kim made two bogeys down the stretch on Saturday but still carded a 3-under 69. She sits at 18-under total, just ahead of Jeeno Thitikul and Yuri Yoshida. She shot a season-high nine birdies to reach 16-under, leaving her only two shots back. She three-putted the par-3 16th after missing a short four-foot putt. Later on the par-5 17th, she scrambled for a birdie from a front bunker. But the 18th hole went wrong. Her approach shot from a six-iron missed left and rolled down a slope into the water. She managed to save bogey, but the lead shrank. “When I was in the second shot … little switch in the wind. That’s all,” Lim said, according to the Killeen Daily Herald . “That’s golf.” Korda’s Hall of Fame Push She started the third round six shots behind the leader. Her final number of 65 showed she is ready to win. Korda needs one more victory this year to qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame. A fifth title would seal her spot in the history books. Korda admitted she feels the momentum building. “Trending every single day, which is what you kind of want going into Sunday,” said Korda, who has posted rounds of 68, 67 and 65. She made a costly mistake on the final hole too. A three-putt bogey from long range stopped her from taking the outright lead. Her approach landed well to the right while the pin was tucked left near a water hazard. “So hopefully I can pull it all together and have a great Sunday,” she added. Thitikul’s Perfect Streak Defending champion Jeeno Thitikul enters the final round. She has not made a single bogey over the last 27 holes. Thitikul shot a 67 on Saturday to sit at 17-under. She also has $8 million in prize money from winning the last two years of this event. Despite her clean card, she lacked birdie opportunities on Saturday. She only converted one chance on the easy par-5 17th. Thitikul knows she needs to be more aggressive to catch Kim. “I don’t think I’m going to change any strategy. top.title: Why was Leny Yoro sent off against Liverpool?
top.description: Life at Manchester United got off to a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as his side was reduced to 10 men inside eight minutes in his managerial bow against Liverpool . Liverpool started brightly and fashioned a chance out of nothing when Ronald Araujo’s hooked clearance left Matthijs de Ligt - making his first league start in a year - in no man’s land. Follow live - Pochettino off to nightmare start as Man Utd manager at Liverpool Alexander Isak latched onto the ball but was clattered into last man Leny Yoro just outside the box, prompting referee Sam Barrett to reach into his pocket and show the Frenchman a red card. Leny Yoro saw red in the early stages of Man United’s clash with Liverpool (PA) "It doesn't matter if you're playing with a back four, or back five, you've got to do the basics right. De Ligt - I'm amazed with him at this level,” Roy Keane said on Sky Sports. "I know he's come back from an injury, he's just not reading the flight of the ball. If you do get it wrong, you run back, you sprint back, and then Yoro has got to be covering. If you're a defender, you always expect the worst." There was a debate over whether VAR should have overturned the decision due to Isak’s heavy touch, which put into question he would have kept control of the ball - a key consideration in determining if a player has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO). "Isak's not getting the ball. There's no way he's getting the ball,” Keane added. "It's clumsy from United. Obviously it's one straight ball over the top. You shouldn't be in so much trouble. "But there's no way he's getting that ball. Absolutely not. I know Isak is quick and he's sharp, but we've looked at it again. "It's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger. But Isak is not getting that ball. Absolutely not." But VAR John Brooks did not call for a review, with the Premier League Match Centre writing in a statement: “The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR. Yoro leaves the pitch after being sent off for Man United (Getty) “REF: ‘It's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO’. “VAR: ‘Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul’.” Things then went from bad to worse for United as Dominik Szoboszlai stepped up to the free-kick and fired past Senne Lammens into the bottom-left corner, ensuring Yoro’s blunder was fully punished. Liverpool doubled their lead just three minutes later, with Florian Wirtz volleying high into the goal as Pochettino’s side rapidly unravelled. Liverpool’s outright domination of the opening stages, combined with losing a defender, sparked Pochettino into making an early change, replacing forward Bryan Mbeumo with centre-back Harry Maguire in the 22nd minute.

top.title: Fox Sports makes donation to Ferris State after 'Big Noon Kickoff'
top.description: Fox Sports left a mark on Ferris State. It also left a check. "Big Noon Kickoff" aired live from the campus in Big Rapids, Mich., on Saturday, Nov. 21, to kick off the start of the Division II playoffs, and the start of Ferris State's drive for a third consecutive national championship. During the two-hour show, Fox Sports also announced a $50,000 donation to the school's athletic department. The donation will go toward the planned future Indoor Activities Complex. The $61.7-million project is scheduled to be constructed in two phases over the next several years, assuming the school meets its ambitious fundraising goal. Fox Sports said its donation will fund a media room at the athletic complex. It will be called the Fox Sports Media Room, and, according to the network, go toward "supporting the next generation of sports storytellers." The donation was among many highlights Saturday, when Ferris State became the first Division II school to host one of college football's premier pregame television shows. A crowd in the thousands lined up early, before sunrise, and was boisterous throughout the show. Many Fox Sports employees called the visit to Big Rapids one of their favorite stops since the show debuted in 2019. "What an awesome day and such a historic day for Ferris State University and Big Rapids," Ferris State head coach Tony Annese said following the Bulldogs' 45-14 win over Missouri-based Truman State before a crowd of more than 8,000. "The credit goes to the students who showed up big, our fans, the staff and the community for supporting us so well." Fox Sports, with the "Big Noon Kickoff" cast including Urban Meyer, Mark Ingram II, Brady Quinn, Matt Leinart, host Rob Stone and reporter Chris Fallica, shined a key spotlight on Ferris State, a small school with an enrollment just under 10,000, and Big Rapids, a city that has a full-time population of even less than that. School administrators hope the spotlight will help spur donations toward the new athletic complex. The first phase of the project is set to include a 134,000-square-foot indoor facility, with a track and training space for all of the school's sports. That includes a football practice field. Additional parking lots are part of the project. The second phase of the project is set to include stadium improvements, including Top Taggart Field lighting, turf and bleachers replacements, plus a 42,000-square-foot support building that will house locker rooms, training space, coaches' offices, fan suites and meeting rooms. In announcing the project earlier this year, Ferris State officials said: "This is more than a facilities upgrade. It’s an investment in people — our student-athletes, our fans, our community." The athletic department added: "Championship culture drives momentum. And momentum demands investment." nigeria.title: FG orders probe into deadly Bayelsa boat accident
nigeria.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has ordered an immediate investigation into the boat accident that claimed several lives in Bayelsa State, warning that it would no longer tolerate avoidable safety violations on the nation’s waterways. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, gave the directive to the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), asking it to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and submit its findings to him. The mishap occurred on Friday, November 20, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser, Dr Bolaji Akinola, Oyetola also directed NIWA to work with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a transparent and comprehensive investigation. The minister described the loss of lives as worrisome and unacceptable, expressing concern over reports that passengers involved in the accident were not wearing life jackets. He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper documentation of passengers was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced. “Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” he said. Oyetola recalled that he visited Bayelsa State on May 2, 2025, where he distributed 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to improve safety on the waterways. He also renewed his call on state governments to gradually phase out wooden boats and replace them with safer and more durable fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation. The minister disclosed that he had contacted Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and families of the victims. He sympathised with the bereaved families and prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died in the accident, while urging stakeholders to work together to prevent a recurrence. nigeria.title: I didn’t politicise it — Gov Yusuf narrates how wife left Kano Govt House
nigeria.description: Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has broken his silence on his marital crisis with wife, Zainab, recounting how she allegedly left the Government House and later initiated divorce proceedings against him in Abuja. The governor, in an interview with BBC Hausa aired on Sunday, said he had remained quiet despite developments in the marriage, which he said had lasted about two decades and produced children. Yusuf said Zainab, a niece of his former political ally, Rabiu Kwankwaso, was previously married before they got together. He recalled that their relationship eventually deteriorated, leading to her departure from the Government House, an experience he said he endured without publicly discussing the matter. “Many things happened, to the point where her belongings were packed and she was taken away from my house, and through it all, I remained patient and did not speak out,” Yusuf said. He said he had tried to reassure their children that their mother would return, but was subsequently taken aback when the matter ended up in court. The governor said he was particularly surprised that the divorce suit was filed in Abuja rather than Kano. “Suddenly, she dragged me to court, a court in Abuja, not even in Kano,” he said. Yusuf described the development as distressing, adding that he had information about the circumstances surrounding his wife’s departure but would not publicly disclose the details. Asked whether he was using the family dispute for political purposes, the governor denied bringing politics into the matter, questioning how anyone in a similar situation would react. “I am not the one who politicised it. If this was done to you, how would you feel?” he asked. He further lamented that his wife’s belongings were removed and she was taken to another residence without his knowledge, before he learnt that she had instituted legal proceedings against him. The marital dispute is before the Upper Area Court in the Gudu District of Abuja, where the divorce case, marked CV/97/26, was adjourned until December 15. The adjournment followed a request by Kano Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who represented Yusuf, for more time to brief the governor on the court proceedings. The crisis has drawn political attention because of Yusuf’s relationship with Kwankwaso, who played a significant role in his political rise. Their relationship reportedly deteriorated after Yusuf defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party to the All Progressives Congress in January 2026, while Kwankwaso later joined the New Nigeria Democratic Congress. nigeria.title: Barcelona fight back from two goals down to beat Villarreal, extend La Liga lead
nigeria.description: Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first half penalty. However the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. “We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I’ll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. “Against a team like this you can’t always turn things around from two down.” The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Fermin Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance to send the visitors ahead. Two minutes later Villarreal doubled their advantage when Tani Oluwaseyi, another Canadian, broke in down the left flank and smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net. Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. Yamal took it himself but dragged his effort against the post and wide. The winger tried to make amends with a burst inside from the wing before half-time but Peter Gulacsi palmed away his cross-shot and the goalkeeper and his defence combined to thwart Eric Garcia on the follow up. – Quickfire treble – Barcelona came out invigorated in the second half and quickly dragged themselves back into the match. Pedri shot wide and Gulacsi saved from Lopez’s low effort before Martin found the net in the 57th minute. Pedri crossed the ball in from the left for the defender to head home. Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro. Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily. Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, ninth, left frustrated. “The (first Barca) goal psychologically killed us, they gained confidence, a couple of minutes later they equalised and from there it’s a lot more difficult,” Comesana told DAZN. Later Sunday Atletico Madrid, third, visit Getafe among other fixtures. Vanguard News The post Barcelona

nigeria.title: Crude supply to refineries hits 179.31m barrels in 10 months
nigeria.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Crude oil supply to domestic refineries in Nigeria reached 179.31 million barrels between January and October 2026, with local production accounting for 144.97 million barrels and imports contributing 34.33 million barrels. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), in its October 2026 Midstream and Downstream Statistics, disclosed that crude oil supply to refineries rose to 22.8 million barrels in October, from 18.53 million barrels in September. The October figure represented a 23.1 per cent increase month-on-month. A breakdown showed that domestic crude supply increased by 19.8 per cent to 19.13 million barrels in October, from 15.97 million barrels in the preceding month. Similarly, imported crude supply rose by 43.4 per cent to 3.67 million barrels in October, compared with 2.56 million barrels in September. Meanwhile, the daily average receipt of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, increased by 21 per cent to 46.9 million litres per day in October, from 38.7 million litres per day in September. According to the report, domestic refineries supplied an average of 31.9 million litres of petrol daily in October, compared with 28.5 million litres per day in September, representing a 12 per cent increase. Petrol imports also increased by 47 per cent to 15 million litres per day in October, from 10.2 million litres per day in the preceding month. Despite the improvement, total petrol supply remained below the estimated daily demand benchmark of 50 million litres and the 13-month average of 50.2 million litres per day. The report further showed that domestic refineries accounted for 62.6 per cent of the 13-month average petrol supply, while imports contributed 37.4 per cent. A month-by-month breakdown indicated that domestic refinery petrol supply peaked at 41.5 million litres per day in May, while imports reached their highest level of 24.8 million litres per day in January. Combined petrol receipts peaked at 74.2 million litres per day in December 2025 before declining in subsequent months. On other petroleum products, the NMDPRA report showed that daily average receipts of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), commonly known as diesel, increased by 93 per cent to 16.8 million litres per day in October. However, aviation fuel (ATK) receipts declined by 36 per cent to 2.1 million litres per day, while Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) receipts increased by 11 per cent to 5.2 thousand tonnes daily. He stressed that while regional solidarity and respect for the sovereign equality of member states must remain fundamental principles of the Union, these should be appropriately balanced with the relative financial commitments, responsibilities and risks borne by individual member states, particularly in determining participation in decision-making and governance. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. A Vision For Global Recognition Speaking on the success of the festival, Founder and Creative Producer, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “Our ambition has always been to create more than a theatre festival. We want to build a platform that places Lagos firmly on the global cultural map, gives African stories the international visibility they deserve and creates meaningful opportunities for our artists. Welcoming over 20,000 attendees, presenting more than 25 productions and bringing international performers from four countries to Lagos is a powerful affirmation of this vision. Theatre is not just entertainment; it is an instrument of cultural identity, economic opportunity and global influence. The Stage Is Everywhere, and Africa must claim its rightful place on that stage.” A Week Of Culture And Collaboration The festival opened on November 9 with Theatre Meets Food at Kaly Restaurant, featuring celebrated chef Hilda Baci in a unique fusion of culinary artistry and live performance. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. sports.title: Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and sports broadcaster, dies at 75
sports.description: Former football star and famed broadcaster Tom Jackson has died, his family and ESPN announced Sunday. Jackson rose to prominence as a Denver Broncos player and went on to build a career as a beloved NFL analyst for ESPN, becoming a mainstay of the network's Sunday football programs for three decades, including its "Sunday NFL Countdown" show. He was 75. Jimmy Pitaro, the chairman of ESPN, praised Jackson in a statement released by the network after his death. In it, Pitaro called Jackson "one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN's history," who "brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans." "Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends," Pitaro said. "Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure." Jackson's family informed ESPN that he died Friday, but it was their wish that his death not be announced until the start of the network's "Sunday NFL Countdown" show by Jackson's longtime friend and on-air partner Chris Berman. "Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom's was frequent and unmistakable," Berman said at the start of the show. "Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend, too." Berman said Jackson made a surprise visit a couple of weeks ago to ESPN, where he worked for 32 years after playing 14 seasons for the Broncos, and that the two talked on Tuesday. A fourth-round draft pick out of Louisville in 1973, Jackson was the inspirational leader of Denver's first Super Bowl team in 1977. He started 177 games for the Broncos between 1973-86, retiring after the team's second Super Bowl appearance. He was a two-time Associated Press All-Pro and three-time Pro Bowler. Following his playing days, Jackson had a second career at ESPN from 1987-2016 and was featured on "Sunday NFL Countdown" and "NFL Primetime." sports.title: Kirk Cousins on pace to make unique NFL history
sports.description: Nov 24, 2022; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) warms up before the game against the New England Patriots at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-USA TODAY Sports Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins has had a whirlwind month, getting traded from the Las Vegas Raiders back to the franchise where he spent six seasons. Now, that midseason move has put the veteran in position to do something no quarterback has ever done before. Because the Raiders hadn’t yet had their bye week and the Vikings already had theirs, Cousins is on track to become the first quarterback in the modern era to play 18 regular-season games. So far, the 38-year-old reportedly has no objection to the unique opportunity to make NFL history. Cousins Returns to Minnesota The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Raiders just hours before this month’s NFL trade deadline, sending a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas in return. The deal brought the four-time Pro Bowler back to Minnesota, where he played from 2018 to 2023, and put him in line to start for the Vikings right away. It also cleared the way for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take over as the starter in Las Vegas. Cousins had played the first nine games of the season for the Raiders while mentoring the rookie, and star wide receiver Justin Jefferson said that Cousins immediately took charge after rejoining the Vikings. His return got off to a strong start, too. Cousins threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns last Sunday as the Vikings rolled to a 30-10 win over the rival Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Across 10 combined games with Las Vegas and Minnesota, Cousins has completed 64.5% of his passes for 2,547 yards and 22 touchdowns. That has him sixth in the NFL in passing yards and tied with C.J. Stroud for second in touchdown passes, trailing only Joe Burrow’s 27. ‘Hasn’t had a bye week’ The Raiders don’t have their bye until Week 13, while the Vikings already had theirs back in Week 6. That leaves Cousins with no week off this season and a chance to suit up 18 times, starting with Sunday’s game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. That will allow Cousins to make some rather unique NFL history. No quarterback has ever played 18 regular-season games, but a handful of other players have. sports.title: Why was Leny Yoro sent off against Liverpool?
sports.description: Life at Manchester United got off to a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as his side was reduced to 10 men inside eight minutes in his managerial bow against Liverpool . Liverpool started brightly and fashioned a chance out of nothing when Ronald Araujo’s hooked clearance left Matthijs de Ligt - making his first league start in a year - in no man’s land. Follow live - Pochettino off to nightmare start as Man Utd manager at Liverpool Alexander Isak latched onto the ball but was clattered into last man Leny Yoro just outside the box, prompting referee Sam Barrett to reach into his pocket and show the Frenchman a red card. Leny Yoro saw red in the early stages of Man United’s clash with Liverpool (PA) "It doesn't matter if you're playing with a back four, or back five, you've got to do the basics right. De Ligt - I'm amazed with him at this level,” Roy Keane said on Sky Sports. "I know he's come back from an injury, he's just not reading the flight of the ball. If you do get it wrong, you run back, you sprint back, and then Yoro has got to be covering. If you're a defender, you always expect the worst." There was a debate over whether VAR should have overturned the decision due to Isak’s heavy touch, which put into question he would have kept control of the ball - a key consideration in determining if a player has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO). "Isak's not getting the ball. There's no way he's getting the ball,” Keane added. "It's clumsy from United. Obviously it's one straight ball over the top. You shouldn't be in so much trouble. "But there's no way he's getting that ball. Absolutely not. I know Isak is quick and he's sharp, but we've looked at it again. "It's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger. But Isak is not getting that ball. Absolutely not." But VAR John Brooks did not call for a review, with the Premier League Match Centre writing in a statement: “The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR. Yoro leaves the pitch after being sent off for Man United (Getty) “REF: ‘It's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO’. “VAR: ‘Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul’.” Things then went from bad to worse for United as Dominik Szoboszlai stepped up to the free-kick and fired past Senne Lammens into the bottom-left corner, ensuring Yoro’s blunder was fully punished. Liverpool doubled their lead just three minutes later, with Florian Wirtz volleying high into the goal as Pochettino’s side rapidly unravelled. Liverpool’s outright domination of the opening stages, combined with losing a defender, sparked Pochettino into making an early change, replacing forward Bryan Mbeumo with centre-back Harry Maguire in the 22nd minute.

sports.title: Fox Sports makes donation to Ferris State after 'Big Noon Kickoff'
sports.description: Fox Sports left a mark on Ferris State. It also left a check. "Big Noon Kickoff" aired live from the campus in Big Rapids, Mich., on Saturday, Nov. 21, to kick off the start of the Division II playoffs, and the start of Ferris State's drive for a third consecutive national championship. During the two-hour show, Fox Sports also announced a $50,000 donation to the school's athletic department. The donation will go toward the planned future Indoor Activities Complex. The $61.7-million project is scheduled to be constructed in two phases over the next several years, assuming the school meets its ambitious fundraising goal. Fox Sports said its donation will fund a media room at the athletic complex. It will be called the Fox Sports Media Room, and, according to the network, go toward "supporting the next generation of sports storytellers." The donation was among many highlights Saturday, when Ferris State became the first Division II school to host one of college football's premier pregame television shows. A crowd in the thousands lined up early, before sunrise, and was boisterous throughout the show. Many Fox Sports employees called the visit to Big Rapids one of their favorite stops since the show debuted in 2019. "What an awesome day and such a historic day for Ferris State University and Big Rapids," Ferris State head coach Tony Annese said following the Bulldogs' 45-14 win over Missouri-based Truman State before a crowd of more than 8,000. "The credit goes to the students who showed up big, our fans, the staff and the community for supporting us so well." Fox Sports, with the "Big Noon Kickoff" cast including Urban Meyer, Mark Ingram II, Brady Quinn, Matt Leinart, host Rob Stone and reporter Chris Fallica, shined a key spotlight on Ferris State, a small school with an enrollment just under 10,000, and Big Rapids, a city that has a full-time population of even less than that. School administrators hope the spotlight will help spur donations toward the new athletic complex. The first phase of the project is set to include a 134,000-square-foot indoor facility, with a track and training space for all of the school's sports. That includes a football practice field. Additional parking lots are part of the project. The second phase of the project is set to include stadium improvements, including Top Taggart Field lighting, turf and bleachers replacements, plus a 42,000-square-foot support building that will house locker rooms, training space, coaches' offices, fan suites and meeting rooms. In announcing the project earlier this year, Ferris State officials said: "This is more than a facilities upgrade. It’s an investment in people — our student-athletes, our fans, our community." The athletic department added: "Championship culture drives momentum. And momentum demands investment." A BIG NOON visit with a lasting impact. ❤️ @FOXSports is proud to contribute $50,000 toward the new athletics facility at @FerrisState , including a FOX Sports Media Room

technology.description: The computerization of cars comes at a price to US consumers, according to the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), which says that software fees and other charges faced by mechanics push up garage costs. An investigation by the non-profit consumer group estimates that car repair costs for Americans have been inflated by $12 billion each year, as vehicles integrate more computerized functions. Its report, Closing Shop , is available online. To find a failed sensor, release an electronic parking brake, or perform diagnostics, a technician has to first connect a laptop or tablet to the vehicle. To so this, the repair shop has to have the right software tools, and that means paying the vehicle manufacturer subscription charges and other fees, in order to get the information they need to complete the job. If smaller independent repair shops can’t afford all the necessary software or subscriptions, they may be forced to steer customers to authorized dealerships for some fixes – about one in five jobs – and this allows the latter to charge more. PIRG claims that drivers pay for this through their insurance premiums, even if they never need to get their car fixed, because higher repair costs mean higher insurance claims. It says the price of auto insurance has risen three times as fast as the rest of the US economy since 2012. Even if mechanics do choose to pay for the software, they spend an estimated collective 83 million hours a year buying, downloading, logging in, and waiting. At typical repair rates, that adds up to $12 billion. A separate report from the PIRG Education Fund claims that a two-tiered repair model now exists, where independent sites conduct repairs with less information, less powerful diagnostic tools, and higher associated costs than the authorized dealerships. The advocacy group wants to see legislators take this issue in hand, and has a number of recommendations for them. One is to stop manufacturers from locking out independent mechanics from simple repair jobs like changing brake pads, and require them to support a standard protocol for authenticating independent diagnostic tools. science.title: SpaceX sends classified US spy satellites to orbit in early-morning launch from California coast (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the NROL-136 mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office from California on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the U.S. Space Force , and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 is the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo mission becomes 2nd ever to arrive in orbit around Mercury
science.description: null For just the second time ever, Mercury has received a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — arrived in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. Before BepiColombo, just one spacecraft had ever circled the solar system's innermost planet: NASA's MESSENGER , which did so from March 2011 to April 2015. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must therefore shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Saturday's orbital insertion came after a 37-minute-long engine burn, which began at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT). There was a bit drama involved, however, as confirmation of the maneuver's success didn't come for several hours afterward. "We've heard back from Bepi — the spacecraft is now in contact with the ground and the teams at ESOC [the European Space Operations Centre] are busy assessing the telemetry. Flight Dynamics already has confirmed it achieved orbital capture around Mercury! Early next week we'll share the next update with the upcoming steps," the mission team said via X on Saturday evening. science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

science.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
science.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . It's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns

science.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
science.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue." science.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
science.description: null For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth. Aldebaran is about 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are roughly 150 light-years distant. The orange eye of Taurus is a foreground star that happens to lie almost exactly along our line of sight toward the Hyades. This fact exposes one of the most convincing tricks in stargazing. The night sky looks flat, and our brains are extremely willing to believe it. But it has incredible depth — and when you can see parts of the night sky in 3D, that's when you begin to appreciate that you're not looking at a flat map. Instead, you begin to see our cosmic neighborhood as it really is. By appreciating depth, you learn its geography. What's happening and when to look Aldebaran, the brightest star in the constellation of Taurus. (Image credit: Christophe Lehenaff via Getty Images) Taurus is now easy to find from the Northern Hemisphere during the evening. Once it's dark, look east for a small, tight knot of stars — the Pleiades open cluster (M45) — and then look nearby for a much larger V-shaped arrangement. That V is the Hyades, with unmistakably orange Aldebaran apparently sitting on one arm. Aldebaran's name is derived from the Arabic Al Dabarān, meaning "the follower," because it appears to trail the Pleiades across the night sky. The Hyades is a real physical group of stars — an open cluster — that formed together and moves through our galaxy together. About 153 light-years away, the Hyades is the nearest open star cluster to Earth. The name means "the rainmakers" because their rising and setting times in the ancient Greek sky coincided with wet weather. The stars in the Hyades are of a similar age — and mostly sun-like stars, or similar — so astronomers can tell that they all formed together in the same nebula . Orange-red star Aldebaran — the 14th-brightest star in the night sky — is the interloper, sitting less than half as far away from the sun . If you could somehow view the neighborhood from another part of the Milky Way , the familiar arrangement would fall apart. Aldebaran would no longer sit conveniently in the bull's face, and Taurus itself would stop looking like a bull. Constellations aren't objects in the same sense as a planet or star cluster.
